thread:
lena: Heads-up — I ran into a confusing 429 example in the error reference while porting the SDK snippets. The current example shows a naive retry loop that will hammer us.

matt: ah ok, which file/line?

lena: docs/error-reference/429-behavior.md, section 'quick retry'. Suggest we replace with a backoff + Retry-After handling example.

ali: +1. Also the curl sample doesn't include the Retry-After header parsing, which is important for clients. Want to propose a small repro snippet?

lena: yep, here's what I pasted into the playground to reproduce the simple scenario (dev-only):

```
# simulate: keep sending peak requests
for i in range(30):
  r = requests.post(API, json={"input": "spam"})
  if r.status_code == 429:
    print('retry-after', r.headers.get('Retry-After'))
  sleep(0.2)
```

matt: that matches what QA saw. They hit a short window of surge + 429s, and our docs should show graceful degrade: exponential backoff with jitter, and fallbacks to smaller models.

sophie: I can draft a new snippet showing both server-sent Retry-After handling and an SDK-friendly pattern (pseudocode). Want it to be tiny — one block for curl, one for python SDK.

ali: include note about context-trimming as an alternative fallback (suggested text: "If Retry-After is long or absent, consider trimming non-essential context and retrying; prefer circuit-breaker behavior to avoid queues").

lena: exactly. Also add a short entry explaining how to use our Retry-After header in client backoff windows vs. purely exponential timers. Some customers misinterpret it as a suggestion rather than a directive.

matt: OK — docs PR path: please target docs/error-reference/429-behavior.md. Label with '429-playbook' and 'needs-approval'.

ali: drafting now. Quick question: do we want to show the SDK pattern using the unified retry header we just shipped (X-Redwood-Retry)? Or keep to standard Retry-After only?

sophie: include both. Example: prefer Retry-After if present, else fall back to X-Redwood-Retry suggestions, else exponential+jitter. Keep examples compact.

lena: can you add a short testable curl example? Something like:

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/respond \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -d '{"prompt":"short"}'
# check headers for Retry-After or X-Redwood-Retry
```

ali: I'll add a one-liner shell that parses Retry-After and sleeps: `sleep $(curl -sI ... | grep -i Retry-After | awk '{print $2}')` — but annotate it's simplified and brittle.

matt: good call. Also add a short troubleshooting checklist at the end: 1) check model fallback policy, 2) confirm autoscale capacity/state, 3) inspect per-token latency graphs, 4) check for upstream rate limiting.

lena: will add that. One more thing: link to the SDK snippet files in /sdk-snippets/ so maintainers can keep parity. We have to update python, js, and go.

sophie: I'll open the PR with all three mini-snippets. Draft title: "429 playbook: Retry-After and graceful fallback examples". Anyone object?

matt: fine. Tagging reviewers: @ali @lena.

docs-bot: PR created by sophie: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/873 — title: "429 playbook: Retry-After and graceful fallback examples". Labels: docs, 429-playbook, needs-approval.

ali: checking now. Quick nit — we should avoid telling users to always sleep for Retry-After if value is < 1s; we should normalize to minimum 1s and add jitter.

lena: yup note that. Also add guidance for streaming responses: "If streaming is interrupted by a 429, prefer reconnect with backoff and reattach partial context where possible; avoid resending full prompt blindly."

matt: approved in principle. Sophie, can you include a short 'how we tested this' section with the small script and expected behavior? That'll help QA sign off.

sophie: will do. PR should be ready in ~30m. I'll ping you both for review before merging.

deploy-bot: staging docs site build queued (build #12478).

ali: thanks — once merged, please also update the changelog snippet for the nightly. We want this surfaced in the next docs digest.

lena: noted. After the merge I'll create a quick FAQ blurb to add to the top-level troubleshooting hub.

matt: cool. If QA sees anything flaky, we'll convert the example to a small integration test.

sophie: PR is up and I've requested reviews from @ali and @lena. Leaving minor TODOs inline.

lena: saw it, reviewing now. :thumbsup:

ali: one small suggestion pushed. Looks good to me.

sophie: merged after quick fixes. deploy-bot: deploy preview published at https://docs-preview.redwood.com/429-playbook.
